sources.title: The Display of Esarhaddon’s Succession Treaty at Kalḫu as a Means of Internal Political Control
sources.institution: Cristina Barcina; Antiguo Oriente 14 (2016), pp. 11–52; Pontificia Universidad Católica Argentina repository
sources.locator: Printed pp. 11–16 (PDF pages 1–6), especially introduction pp. 12–13 and purpose p. 15. Text read; no independent examination of tablets.
sources.originalChronology: The article dates the succession oaths to 672 BCE; no modern day is inferred.
sources.scopedClaim: The oath arrangements sought loyalty to Ashurbanipal. Preserved tablets and letters concern different groups of participants.
sources.reuseTerms: Reference only; no source prose or images redistributed

date.noteEn: This dates the succession oaths, not Ashurbanipal's accession. Barcina distinguishes the oath-takers named in tablets from citizens mentioned in correspondence. The article's interpretation of the king's hidden motives is not treated as established fact.

events.titleEn: Esarhaddon binds oath-takers to his chosen successor
events.summaryEn: Esarhaddon organizes loyalty oaths supporting Ashurbanipal as his successor. The arrangements extend to Assyrian participants and eastern city-lords; a surviving provincial version names a governor and administrative and military groups.
events.geographyEn: Assyria and its provincial sphere, including Kalḫu and Kullania
events.selectionNote: A major regional succession arrangement, distinct from the existing Thebes campaign, Nineveh's destruction and Jerwan's aqueduct. This records a political decision rather than the modern discovery of a tablet. It does not assert universal compliance, successful conflict prevention or a first use of loyalty oaths.

review.reviewedBy: Codex independent source and English check; independent final data, English and integration review
